sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 6.2% a year from $26.6 billion in FY2016 to $45.7 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F157], but the path was a full cycle rather than a straight line.
Revenue rose 25.6% in FY2018 to $37.4 billion [F3][D93], then climbed 16.5% in FY2023 to a peak of $61.3 billion [F8][D322] before falling 15.6% in FY2024 and 11.7% in FY2025 [D367][D412].
The FY2018 step came largely from the Wirtgen acquisition, which added 12% to net sales for the year [P72].
The FY2024 decline reflected lower shipment volumes across every equipment segment, driven by rising grain stocks, lower commodity prices, elevated interest rates and inventory management [P17].
Operating margin peaked at 21.2% in FY2023 [F29] and has since fallen to 17.5% in FY2024 [F30], while net income fell 29.2% in FY2025 to $5.0 billion [F40][D413].
Production & Precision Agriculture is the largest segment at 38.9% of FY2025 revenue [D867], and it subtracted 7.0pp from growth as sales fell 17.0% [D868][D869].
PPA sales volumes fell 30% in the U.S. and Canada, partly offset by a 22% increase in Brazil, with price realization up 1% in the U.S. and Canada [P10].
Construction & Forestry, 25.5% of revenue [D889], fell 11.8% and subtracted 3.0pp [D890][D891], while Small Agriculture & Turf fell 7.0% and subtracted 1.5pp [D906][D907].

Profit grew far faster than revenue over the window: operating income compounded at 16.9% to FY2024 against 6.2% revenue growth [F159][F157], and incremental operating margin was 43.7% in FY2021 and 39.8% in FY2023 [D253][D343].
Diluted EPS compounded at 16.1% against net income at 14.2% [F162][F160], as the diluted share count fell from 316.6 million in FY2016 to 271.7 million in FY2025 [X110][X119].
The FY2024 operating margin of 17.5% [F30] sits well above the window median of 12.1% [D1335] but below the FY2023 high of 21.2% [D1334] and far above the FY2016 low of 9.7% [D1333].
In FY2024 the margin fell 3.7pp [D378] as revenue fell faster than operating costs, with revenue growth 3.7pp below operating-cost growth [D389] and SG&A costing 1.9pp [D391].
FY2024 production costs were favorable on lower material and profit-sharing costs, partly offset by higher manufacturing overhead from lower volumes and production inefficiencies [P16].
Net margin fell 2.7pp to 11.0% in FY2025 [F50][D422], below the peer median of 12.7% [D1352], while the effective tax rate eased to 20.1% [D400].
Interest expense of $3.2 billion in FY2025 [X82] against $6.3 billion of pretax income [X92] is the main below-the-line drag.
Operating cash flow of $7.5 billion and free cash flow of $6.1 billion in FY2025 [F80][F100] were 1.48x and 1.21x net income [D401][D402], above the window median of 0.91x for free cash flow [D1347].
FY2025 operating inflows were driven by net income adjusted for non-cash provisions and a decrease in sales receivables, partly offset by an OPEB contribution [P5].
Free cash flow margin was 13.4% in FY2025 [D398], near the peer median of 13.2% [D1354] and above the window median of 11.6% [D1341].
Capex was 3.0% of revenue and 0.61x D&A in FY2025 [D397][D403], down from $1.6 billion in FY2024 [F89] as the capital programme eased.
Net debt was $5.5 billion at FY2025 [D407], or 12.1% of revenue [D408], a far stronger position than the peer median of -38.8% net cash to revenue and the 100th percentile [D1358][D1357].
Cash rose 13.0% to $8.3 billion [F140][D420] while total debt was roughly flat at $13.8 billion [D406], and equity grew 13.6% to $26.0 billion [F156][D421].
Buybacks plus dividends of $2.9 billion absorbed 46.9% of free cash flow in FY2025 [D409][D410], down from 121.9% in FY2023 [D320], and the diluted share count fell 1.9% [D427].
Return on average equity fell to 20.6% in FY2025 [D411], below the peer median of 28.3% and in the 17th percentile [D1362][D1361].
Revenue has now fallen two years running, 15.6% in FY2024 and 11.7% in FY2025 [D367][D412], the most severe and persistent flag [R1].
Production Agriculture, 37.1% of revenue, fell 17.6% in FY2025 [D657][D658][R2], and the overlapping PPA segment fell 17.0% [D868][R3].
The filings attribute the volume decline to moderating market conditions and lower U.S. and Canada volumes, partly offset by Brazil [P10], and Small Agriculture & Turf also cites higher tariffs [P8].
Construction & Forestry, 25.5% of revenue, fell 11.8% [D889][D890][R4], so the weakness is not confined to agriculture.
A data-quality note: FY2017 SG&A was later reported as $3,098.0 million against the $3,066.6 million used here [X34][R8], which does not change any conclusion above.
Whether PPA revenue stabilises above the FY2025 level of $17.8 billion [S213]; a further decline would extend the two-year revenue contraction [R1].
Whether the operating margin holds above the 12.1% window median [D1335] or slides toward the 9.7% FY2016 low [D1333], reported in the FY2026 10-K.
Management expects lower equipment-operations operating cash flow in FY2026 than FY2025, driven by lower net income adjusted for non-cash provisions, partly offset by inventory reductions [P6].
